nodes.title: Effect on the simulation state
nodes.comment: An effect is NOT a state: it is a change applied to ONE variable of the state. Soil, climate and finances share this format; only 'target' changes. Effects are deterministic given their drawn values (see monte_carlo.json).

fields.description: JSON Pointer to the changed variable, relative to the chain node (markov.json#/definitions/node).
add: adds 'value' once. multiply: multiplies by 'value'. set: overwrites. rate: 'value' per day, multiplied by the days spent in the state/action.
Unit of 'value'. For add/set it is the target unit; for rate it is target unit per day; multiply is dimensionless.

When a one-off effect (add/multiply/set) fires inside a state: on entry (e.g. sowing cost) or on exit (e.g. harvest revenue). Ignored for operation=rate, which accumulates over the whole stay, and for effects on transitions, which fire when the edge is crossed.
Conditions on the node (all must hold). Empty/absent = always applies.
Clamp applied to the target after the effect (e.g. N2 >= 0, 3 <= pH <= 9).
Where the number comes from, specific enough to check it: a file and field, a dataset and query, a paper or a rule. Example: 'PAM municipal, year pair 2005-2006'.
JSON Pointer into the node, like 'target'.

nodes.title: Random event
nodes.comment: Part of the ENVIRONMENT, never of the farmer's choice. Monte Carlo draws events from the environment stream, so two scenarios with the same seed see the same events on the same days. While active, an event behaves like a temporary overlay on the current state: 'entry' effects at onset, 'rate' effects for each active day, 'exit' effects when it ends.

nodes.title: Markov chain graph
nodes.comment: The chain walks over DISCRETE states (crop x stage). CONTINUOUS variables (soil, climate, finances) live in the node and change only through effects: what the chain can alter is whatever appears as an effect target. The chain holds no seed and makes no choice by itself: a scenario policy (monte_carlo.json) decides which edge to take, deterministically (rotation) or by drawing from 'probability' (markov).

fields.description: Symmetric Dirichlet prior for the eligible crop destinations. Edge probability is the posterior mean before calendar and environmental adjustment.

nodes.title: Monte Carlo run
nodes.comment: A run separates three things. (1) ENVIRONMENT is random: climate periods, events and uncertain effect values are drawn from streams derived from 'seed' and the trajectory index only, so every scenario sees the same environment (common random numbers). (2) CHOICE belongs to the scenario: a 'rotation' policy is deterministic; a 'markov' policy draws edges from the chain probabilities with its own choice stream, which never shifts the environment streams. (3) OUTCOMES are deterministic given (1) and (2): effects are applied in a fixed order.

node_description: The state of one Monte Carlo trajectory at a point in time: what the field looks like now. Behaviour: (1) Monte Carlo creates one node per trajectory from a profile (soil, climate at day 0, finances at 0). (2) Entering a state applies its 'entry' effects. (3) While in the state, 'rate' effects accumulate over duration_days and Monte Carlo refreshes climate each period. (4) Leaving applies 'exit' effects. (5) Outgoing edges are filtered by 'when' against the node, one is drawn, its effects apply, and the loop repeats until the horizon. Why it exists: crops, actions and climate must affect each other (soybean adds N used by maize, liming unlocks soybean, drought cuts yield). They can only do that through one shared place. A field belongs here only if some effect writes it or some condition reads it.
